The Kotlin twin is WHOOP5_HISTORICAL_VERSIONS_WITH_OWN_STREAM in HistoricalLayoutSupport.kt, which has to be a `private val`: the value is a Set, so Kotlin cannot express it as the `const val` the ledger pairs constants on. The internal insert overload gained the two #2847 ECG retention caps as parameters, moving its arity from 6 to 8. Kotlin's WhoopRepository.insert gained the same two in the same change, so the arity moved in lockstep, but the ledger does not pair StreamStore.swift with WhoopRepository.kt and no arity of this function has ever formed a pair. The caps are parameters so a test can prove the rolling delete with a small cap instead of writing tens of thousands of rows.

Structural equals on EcgWaveformSampleEntity (#2847). A Kotlin data class holding a ByteArray needs hand-written equals/hashCode, because the generated ones compare array identity and break every round-trip assertion. Swift's EcgWaveformSample holds [UInt8], which is Equatable by value, so there is no Swift declaration to pair with; PpgWaveformSampleEntity carries the same pair.

Structural hashCode on EcgWaveformSampleEntity (#2847), written for the same reason as its equals: a ByteArray member makes the generated hashCode identity-based. Swift's [UInt8] hashes by value, so there is no Swift declaration to pair with.

Private helper that performs every DAO write for one decoded chunk inside the Room transaction insert opens; it gained the two #2847 ECG retention caps with its caller. Room transactions are opened by a suspending withTransaction block on this platform, where GRDB's syncWrite takes a closure inside StreamStore.insert itself, so there is no Swift function to pair with.

A LOCAL binding inside the private v16 ECG decoder (#2847), not a static constant. The ledger's Swift rule treats any four-space `let` in a file-scope function as a candidate `static let`, which is how it finds file-scope constants without parsing, so a local in a top-level `private func` lands in the inventory. The Kotlin twin's equivalent is a local `val` in its own decodeWhoop5HistoricalV16, which the Kotlin rule never inventories because it matches `const val` only, and a Set-valued or object-valued local cannot be `const` in Kotlin at all. There is nothing to pair and nothing to change in either decoder.

Android evaluates the same autoSync and interval conditions inline in com.noop.garmin.GarminSync.maybeAutoSync, which also launches the sync, so there is no pure Kotlin function to pair.

Maps an HTTP status to the typed GarminApi.Failure that the Apple app target turns into text. Android has no typed failure: com.noop.garmin.GarminApiClient maps the same 401/403, 429 and other-status classes straight to user text (errorMessage) and to a fatal flag (GarminApiException.isFatal), so no single Kotlin function has this contract.

A local func nested inside GarminApi.parseStartTimeGMT that reads one fixed-width digit field of the hand-parsed timestamp. Its Kotlin twin GarminApiClient.parseGmt parses through java.time DateTimeFormatter instead, so there is no digit-field helper on Android.

Civil-date-to-epoch-days step of the hand-written, locale-free GarminApi.parseStartTimeGMT (Foundation date parsing would depend on the device calendar). Its Kotlin twin GarminApiClient.parseGmt uses java.time LocalDateTime.toEpochSecond, which needs no such helper.

Kotlin has no standard round-half-away-from-zero (Math.round rounds half up, kotlin.math.round rounds half to even), so this reimplements Swift's rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero). The Swift side calls that standard-library rounding inline, so there is no Swift function to pair.
